To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 3d U Net architecture performs best for the considered task of grain wise segmentation and that the network can be successfully trained with only a small subset of the available data.

a 3D CNN is the best performing architecture for the considered segmentation problem, that a CNN can also be trained with data from a single time step only and that the resulting segmentation quality is similar to that of the segmentation obtained with a CNN that is trained with data from all time steps.

the combination of CNNs with conventional image processing techniques can be used to segment tomographic image data of functional materials and that the quality of the resulting segmentations is comparable to those obtained from ground truth data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of machine learning methods to tomographic image data of materials.
a new approach for the segmentation of tomographic image data of functional materials, where the grain wise segmentation is achieved by combining CNNs and conventional image processing techniques.
the development of a robust, automated, fast and efficient segmentation method which is able to process large amounts of data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3 D U Net is the best performing network for this application.

a 3D CNN trained with a low resolution CT series and a 3DXRD scan from the last time step is able to segment the entire series of low resolution CT scans with a similar quality as a 3D or 2D CNN trained with the entire CT series.
the 3DX RD data can serve as a good training data set for the segmentation of tomographic image data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

machine learning techniques are a promising approach for enhancing the quality of grain boundaries in CT data and that the resulting enhanced grain boundary images can be used for grain wise segmentation of CT scans.
the combination of 3D CNNs and marker based image processing steps can be used for the segmentation of tomographic image data with poorly visible grain boundaries.
machine learning methods in combination with image processing methods can be successfully used for the segmentation of tomographic image data of materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of machine learning methods and traditional image processing techniques is an effective approach for the segmentation of tomographic image data of materials.
machine learning methods can help to overcome limitations of conventional image processing methods, in particular for the segmentation of poorly visible features.

machine learning methods can be successfully used to enhance poorly visible grain boundaries of tomographic image data of functional materials and that the enhanced grain boundary images can be used as input for subsequent image processing steps.
